messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Patel <jamie.patel@acme.com>, acme-cloud-infra@acme.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC — control plane orchestration & annotated reference diagrams (readout)

Hi Jamie / Acme infra team,

Thanks for taking time yesterday. Attached is a condensed readout of the control-plane / data-plane orchestration we discussed, plus an annotated reference diagram that highlights tenant boundary enforcement points and handoff interfaces. The goal with this note is to capture the decisions you asked for so your network/security teams have a single artifact to review.

Key highlights (TL;DR):
- Control-plane (management APIs, cert propagation, telemetry) will live in a customer-dedicated control plane running in their VPC with a private peering link to our control endpoint (mutual TLS + IP allowlist).
- Data-plane (inference runtime) will be colocated in customer on-prem racks or VPC-hosted GPU pools; traffic between app frontends and runtime will traverse a dedicated egress path that we label as "tenant-egress-proxy".
- We propose a minimal mesh for the control-plane agents to avoid NAT hairpins; see diagram for connector placement.

Open questions for Acme to confirm:
1) Will you accept our connector pattern (outbound TLS-only) or do you require an inbound firewall ACL for the control plane?
2) Is KMS-backed key access via your HSM allowed from our control-plane subnet?
3) Any preferred subnet allocation constraints for the tenant-egress-proxy?

Next steps: if the artifacts look good, Kimberly and Jonas will produce a one-page runbook snippet for your ops team and we can schedule a 30-min follow-up for cutover windows.

Attachments: vpc-orchestration-annotated.png, control-dataflow-v2.vsdx, tenant-boundary-matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Jamie Patel <jamie.patel@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-cloud-infra@acme.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — control plane orchestration & annotated reference diagrams (readout)

Logan,

Thanks for the summary — the diagram helped. Quick answers inline: 
1) We'd prefer outbound-only connectors where possible. Our security team will only permit inbound connections after a completed network review and a signed commitment. Outbound TLS-only matches our current posture.
2) HSM access: we can provide a dedicated service account and allowlist for the control-plane subnet. Need the exact CIDR you'll originate from.
3) Subnet constraints: keep the tenant-egress-proxy within 10.240.0.0/22 for staging and 10.241.0.0/22 for prod.

A couple of asks from our side: can you add a short diagram showing the certificate rotation flow (control plane -> connector -> runtime)? Also, show what failure modes look like if the control-plane loses reachability for 15+ minutes.

Happy to meet Wed afternoon to walk through updates.

—Jamie
Jamie Patel
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Financial
jamie.patel@acme.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Patel <jamie.patel@acme.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-03T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — control plane orchestration & annotated reference diagrams (readout)

Jamie — great notes. I'll take point on the cert rotation sequence and the degraded-mode behavior. A few implementation clarifications from our ops playbook: 
- Cert rotation: control plane will push a new cert bundle to the connector endpoints; connectors validate signed chain from your KMS-backed signing key before swapping. We will include a 5-min overlap window for TLS acceptance to avoid handshake failures during rotation. Diagram attached (runbook-snippets.md) and I'll produce the single-slide sequence you asked for.
- Degraded mode: if control-plane reachability is lost, the runtime will continue to serve cached KV (model kv and prefix caches) for up to X hours based on the last successful policy fetch. Control operations (new model rollout, billing telemetry) will queue and reconcile once connectivity returns. We will add a fail-open vs fail-closed matrix for each operation in the next revision.

Action items I own:
- Produce cert-rotation swimlane + failure scenarios (deliver by 9/04 EOD).
- Update the tenant-boundary spreadsheet with concrete ACL examples for the tenant-egress-proxy.

Logan — do you still want Jonas to diagram the NAT-less connector layout for your network team?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. PM, Deployments — Redwood Inference
